draft.title: Why variation helps a species survive
card: Sexual reproduction mixes the features of two parents, so offspring differ from each other. This difference is called variation.
If the environment changes, for example a new disease arrives, some varied offspring may have features that help them survive. They can then breed and pass those features on.
Asexual offspring are identical to their parent. If a new disease harms one of them, it can harm them all, so a whole group may die.
In a stable place, asexual reproduction can be an advantage. One parent can make offspring quickly without finding a mate, and the offspring suit the place as well as the parent does.
draft.remember: Variation makes it more likely that some survive a change. Asexual reproduction is quick when conditions stay the same.

a.q: A new disease spreads through a field of identical plants grown from one parent. Why might all of the plants die?
opts: They are identical, so none may have a feature to resist it
They are too crowded, so the disease spreads to every plant
They have no variation in size, so they grow too slowly
They came from one parent, so they cannot make seeds
a.why: Identical plants share the same features, so if the disease harms one it can harm all. Crowding might help a disease spread, but it is not the reason the whole group lacks any resistant plant.
a.clue: Think about what identical offspring have in common.

b.q: A fungus grows by asexual reproduction on one farm with steady conditions. Another species reproduces sexually. Which statement best compares them?
opts: The fungus spreads fast here but is at risk if things change
The fungus is safer from disease because it has no variation
The sexual species spreads faster because it needs no mate
The sexual species is at risk because its offspring differ
b.why: With one parent and no mate to find, asexual reproduction can be fast in a stable place. Identical offspring are all at risk if conditions change. Identical offspring do not give safety from disease, because one disease can harm them all.
b.clue: Ask what happens to identical offspring if the place changes.

a.best: They are identical, so none may have a feature to resist it

b.best: The fungus spreads fast here but is at risk if things change

problems.detail: The right option stands out. It is the longest and the only one with two balanced clauses and a qualifier ('here', 'if things change'), so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.
